name: Monthly financial close for one legal entity
summary: Every month the accounting team closes the books of the legal entity so the group can report its results. After cut-off, AP, billing, inventory, payroll and fixed asset owners close their sub-ledgers, the senior accountant books accruals with input from department managers, and staff accountants reconcile about 70 balance sheet accounts. Reviews by the accounting manager, a flux analysis, the controller and the entity finance director each send some work back as adjustments before the package is loaded into group consolidation. The close is slow where it depends on late inputs from departments and other entities, manual spreadsheet reconciliations and sequential review layers.

baseline.org_archetype: A US operating legal entity of a mid-size group (about 800 employees, $300 to $400 million revenue) with an ERP, spreadsheet reconciliations and a group consolidation tool, reporting to the group on about working day 5.
baseline.notes: A normal month. Quarter-end closes add tax, disclosure and sub-certification work; the year-end close adds audit support and takes much longer.

unit_of_work: one monthly close of one legal entity
trigger: The last business day of the month (period end).
end_state: The entity's reporting package is submitted to group consolidation and the period is locked in the ERP, with any group queries answered.

volume.seasonality: Twelve closes a year; quarter-end closes take one or two days longer and the year-end close takes two to four weeks with audit support (cfo_yearend reports site-level annual close medians of 10 to 23 days by company size).

evidence.note: One close per entity per month by definition.

produces.object: entity reporting package and trial balance
monthly financial statements and variance commentary
tax provision and sales tax accruals

systems.name: ERP general ledger and sub-ledgers (AP, AR, inventory, fixed assets)
Shared drive for close support and evidence

steps.name: Confirm cut-off and open the close checklist
steps.description: On the last business day the accounting manager confirms the last shipping and receiving documents of the month with the warehouse, reminds departments of deadlines for invoices, timesheets and accrual inputs, and rolls the close checklist and calendar forward with owners and due days.

error.defect_description: A late shipment or receipt falls into the wrong month

control.basis: Period-end cut-off so revenue and expenses are recorded in the right period (US GAAP accrual accounting, ASC 606 for revenue)

evidence.note: Month-end checklist and communicated cut-off dates (cfo_close); close calendar with cut-off times and close instructions (jofa_2011). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Close the AP sub-ledger and accrue goods received not invoiced
steps.description: The AP specialist posts the last supplier invoices received by cut-off, runs the goods-received-not-invoiced report, prepares the received-not-invoiced accrual listing for the senior accountant, and closes the AP period. Work starts on the first working day, which may be after a weekend.

error.defect_description: Received-not-invoiced listing includes items already invoiced

evidence.note: Sub-ledgers reconciled to the general ledger (tipalti_close); PCF 9.6.1.5 process financial accruals and reversals. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Close the billing and AR sub-ledger
steps.description: The billing and AR specialist runs the final billing for shipments through period end, lists shipped but unbilled orders, applies cash received through the last day, runs the AR aging and the bad debt reserve inputs, and closes the AR period.

error.defect_description: Shipped orders left unbilled or cash applied to the wrong period

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Close inventory and cost accounting
steps.description: The cost accountant checks that all receipts, issues and production are posted, books cycle count adjustments, runs standard cost variance and overhead absorption reports, reviews work in progress and calculates the excess and obsolete inventory reserve.

error.defect_description: Variance capitalised or expensed wrongly, or reserve miscalculated

evidence.note: Inventory valuation and obsolete stock in the close (tipalti_close). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Close payroll, fixed assets and prepaids
steps.description: The staff accountant calculates the payroll accrual for days worked but unpaid and the vacation accrual, runs depreciation and moves finished construction-in-progress to assets, and amortises prepaid expenses from the schedules.

error.defect_description: Payroll accrual days counted wrongly or asset placed in service late

evidence.note: Depreciation and fixed assets in the close (tipalti_close). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Request accrual inputs from department managers
steps.description: The staff accountant emails each department manager a template listing open purchase orders and recurring services and asks for services received but not yet invoiced, such as legal, consulting, marketing and utilities, with a deadline of the second working day.

error.defect_description: None introduced

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Department managers provide accrual estimates
steps.description: About eight department managers check their contracts and vendor activity and reply with estimates for work received but not invoiced. Replies come late or incomplete, and some managers do not reply at all.

error.defect_description: Estimate missing or wrong because the manager does not track vendor work

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Chase missing accrual inputs
steps.description: The staff accountant follows up by email or phone with managers who have not replied, and where no answer comes by the cut-off uses the run rate or the open purchase order to estimate the accrual.

error.defect_description: Run-rate estimate misses a one-off cost

next.condition: accountant estimates from run rate or open PO

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Prepare accrual and adjusting journal entries
steps.description: The senior accountant calculates accruals from the received-not-invoiced listing, unbilled revenue, payroll, department estimates, bonus, interest and rent, checks prior-month auto-reversals, and prepares each journal entry with support in the standard template.

error.defect_description: Accrual duplicated with an invoice already posted, miscalculated or booked to the wrong account

evidence.note: PCF 9.3.2.2 process journal entries and 9.3.2.4 period end adjustments; standard JE templates (jofa_2011). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Review and approve journal entries
steps.description: The accounting manager opens each manual journal entry with its support, checks the calculation, accounts, period and amount against expectations, and approves it in the ERP or returns it with comments. The preparer cannot approve their own entries.

error.defect_description: An incorrect entry is approved

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 for public issuers): manual journal entries independently reviewed and approved by someone other than the preparer

evidence.note: Journal entry checklist with independent review of posted entries as a detective control (jofa_2011). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Post entries and run the preliminary trial balance
steps.description: The senior accountant uploads the approved journal entries, runs the preliminary trial balance, confirms that it balances and that the AP, AR, inventory and fixed asset sub-ledgers agree to their control accounts.

error.defect_description: Upload posts to the wrong period

evidence.note: Trial balance check (wiki_fcm); PCF 9.3.2.8 prepare trial balance. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Reconcile intercompany balances
steps.description: The senior accountant books intercompany charges such as management fees and shared services, compares intercompany receivables, payables and charges with the counterpart entities' figures from the group schedule, and flags differences.

error.defect_description: Intercompany charge booked in only one entity

control.basis: Group intercompany accounting policy: balances agreed with counterparties before submission so they eliminate on consolidation

next.condition: differences to resolve with the counterpart

evidence.note: PCF 9.3.2.5 post and reconcile intercompany transactions. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Wait for counterpart entity to confirm or correct
steps.description: The counterpart entity's accountant checks the difference, usually a charge booked in one entity only or at a different exchange rate, and corrects their books or confirms ours. The case waits on another team in the group.

error.defect_description: None introduced

evidence.note: Counterpart response time is an author estimate; their hands-on time sits in their own entity's close.

steps.name: Prepare balance sheet account reconciliations
steps.description: The staff accountants reconcile about 70 balance sheet accounts: the bank accounts against bank statements, then receivables, inventory, prepaids, fixed assets, accruals, payables, payroll liabilities and tax accounts against sub-ledgers and schedules, and document each reconciling item in the workbook.

error.defect_description: Reconciling item left unexplained or rolled forward, or a reconciliation not tied to the ledger

evidence.note: APQC median of 4 hours to reconcile one bank account (cfo_bankrec) and 6 hours median for general ledger reconciliation (cfo_glrec); this file assumes 4 to 6 bank accounts at 2.5 to 4 hours plus about 65 other accounts at 10 to 30 minutes. Starting with cash follows tipalti_close.

steps.name: Review account reconciliations
steps.description: The accounting manager reviews each reconciliation, focusing on high-risk accounts and aged or unexplained reconciling items, signs it off in the workbook, and returns any that do not tie or lack support.

error.defect_description: Reconciliation signed off with an unsupported item

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 for public issuers): balance sheet reconciliations reviewed and signed off each period

evidence.note: Key controls documented and tested (jofa_2011). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Calculate monthly tax provision and sales tax accruals
steps.description: The tax accountant estimates the month's income tax provision from pre-tax income and the expected annual rate, updates sales and use tax and property tax accruals, and sends the entries to the senior accountant.
outputs: tax provision and tax accrual entries

error.defect_description: Rate or permanent difference misapplied

control.basis: Group reporting policy: monthly estimate of income tax expense under ASC 740 for management reporting (required at quarter-end for public issuers)

evidence.note: Monthly tax provision estimates are common in groups that report monthly; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Run flux analysis and draft commentary
steps.description: The financial analyst compares each income statement and balance sheet line with the prior month, budget and prior year, investigates variances above the thresholds by asking accountants and operations, and drafts the commentary. Unexplained swings often reveal a missed accrual or misposting.

error.defect_description: A real misstatement explained away as timing

control.basis: Management review control: fluctuation analysis against set thresholds before financial statements are released

evidence.note: Fluctuation analysis comparing periods (wiki_fcm); comparison with prior periods and investigation of large variances (jofa_2011). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Draft post-close adjusting entries
steps.description: The senior accountant prepares adjusting entries for errors found in reconciliation review, flux analysis or the controller's review, such as a missed accrual, a misclassification or a reserve change, with support.

error.defect_description: Adjustment itself is wrong

evidence.note: Approval process for post-close adjustments (jofa_2011). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Approve adjusting entries
steps.description: The accounting manager reviews each adjusting entry and its support against the materiality thresholds and approves it for posting, or escalates large ones to the controller.

error.defect_description: None introduced

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 for public issuers): post-close adjustments approved by someone other than the preparer within materiality thresholds

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Controller reviews trial balance and draft financial statements
steps.description: The controller reviews the trial balance, the reconciliation status, the flux commentary and the key judgements on reserves and accruals, and either signs off or asks for changes or more explanation.

error.defect_description: A misstatement passes review

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting (SOX 404 for public issuers): management review of period-end financial statements by someone not involved in preparing them

evidence.note: Final review by a controller or finance manager not involved in the close (tipalti_close). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Prepare the reporting package and load it to group consolidation
steps.description: The financial analyst maps the trial balance to the group chart of accounts, loads it into the consolidation tool, and fills the package: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, intercompany schedule, headcount and KPI schedules, and variance commentary.

error.defect_description: Mapping error or schedule that does not tie to the trial balance

evidence.note: PCF 9.3.4.1 prepare business unit financial statements; spreadsheets and manual touchpoints lengthen consolidation (cfo_consol). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Run group validation checks
steps.description: The consolidation tool runs its validation rules on submission: the package balances, schedules tie to the trial balance, and intercompany balances match the counterparts within tolerance.

error.defect_description: None introduced

evidence.note: Automated validation rules are standard in consolidation tools; failure share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Fix validation errors
steps.description: The senior accountant reads the validation report, corrects mapping errors or schedule differences, agrees remaining intercompany differences with the counterpart, and resubmits the package.

error.defect_description: None introduced

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Finance director reviews and signs off the package
steps.description: The entity finance director reads the package and commentary, questions large variances and judgements, and signs it off for submission. At quarter-end this sign-off becomes the sub-certification that supports the group's certifications.

error.defect_description: None introduced

control.basis: Group reporting policy: entity finance lead signs off the monthly package (quarterly sub-certification supports officer certifications at public groups)

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Submit the package and lock the period
steps.description: The accounting manager submits the package in the consolidation tool by the group deadline and hard-closes the period in the ERP so no further entries can post to it.

error.defect_description: None introduced

control.basis: Hard close: posting periods locked after sign-off; reopening needs controller approval

evidence.note: Group deadlines and sub-ledger posting discipline (cfo_close). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Answer group reporting queries
steps.description: The senior accountant answers questions from the group reporting team about variances, intercompany differences or classifications, and sends supporting schedules. Rarely the group books a top-side adjustment instead of reopening the period.

error.defect_description: None introduced

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one US operating entity of a mid-size group (about $300 to $400 million revenue) closing in an ERP with spreadsheet reconciliations in 2019 to 2022.

exceptions.name: Late accrual inputs
exceptions.description: Department managers miss the accrual deadline; the accountant chases and estimates from run rate or open POs.

exceptions.name: Journal entries returned
exceptions.description: The accounting manager returns entries with errors for correction before posting.

exceptions.name: Intercompany differences
exceptions.description: Balances with other group entities do not agree and wait on the counterpart's correction.

exceptions.name: Reconciliations returned
exceptions.description: Reconciliations that do not tie or lack support go back to the preparer.

exceptions.name: Post-close adjustments
exceptions.description: Flux analysis, controller review or the finance director find errors that need adjusting entries and another review.

exceptions.name: Group validation failure
exceptions.description: The consolidation tool rejects the package for mapping or intercompany differences.

exceptions.name: Group queries
exceptions.description: Group reporting asks questions after submission.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from running the trial balance to completed consolidated statements
benchmarks.population: APQC General Accounting Open Standards Benchmarking, 2,300 organisations (as cited)

evidence.note: p50 is the APQC median. p90 is an author estimate above the bottom-quarter threshold of 10 days. The APQC measure starts at the trial balance, so it excludes the sub-ledger close days included in this workflow.
The article does not say whether this is per account or per close.

pain_points.description: Accrual inputs from department managers arrive late or not at all, so accountants chase and estimate, and misses show up later as flux surprises.

evidence.note: Author's reading of common practice; consistent with dependence on other teams named in cfo_bankrec.

pain_points.description: About 70 reconciliations are prepared by hand in spreadsheets in the same few days, which is the largest block of hands-on time and the main source of unexplained items.
Sequential review layers (accounting manager, controller, finance director) each wait on the reviewer's calendar and each can send work back to adjusting entries.
Intercompany differences wait on other entities and resurface as group validation failures.
Close coordination runs on checklists, email chains and status meetings rather than a system, so status is hard to see.

sources.title: Metric of the Month: cycle time for monthly close (citing APQC General Accounting Open Standards Benchmarking)
sources.supports: Median 6.4 calendar days from running the trial balance to completing consolidated financial statements (2,300 organisations); top quarter 4.8 days or less, bottom quarter 10 or more days. A standard chart of accounts saves about two days; pre-close reconciliations and journal entries, a month-end checklist, communicated cut-off dates and sub-ledgers posting summaries reduce close time.

sources.title: Best organizations report consolidated financials in 4 days: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Calendar days from running the initial monthly entity trial balance to completing consolidated statements: 25th percentile 4 days, 75th percentile 10 days; excessive spreadsheets, manual touchpoints, human error and non-standard charts of accounts lengthen it.

sources.title: How long is too long to reconcile the general ledger? Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Hours accounting staff take to reconcile the general ledger: median 6, 25th percentile 5, 75th percentile 10; liability and revenue accounts that need tracing to source documents and monthly rather than continuous reconciliation take longer.

sources.title: What bank reconciliation cycle time really tells you: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Time to reconcile a single bank account: top performers about 2.6 hours, median 4 hours, bottom performers 5 hours or more; month-end surges, unmatched receipts, paper checks and dependence on other teams slow it.

sources.title: 5 ways to speed up period-end management reports: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Cycle time to produce period-end management reports: top quarter 6 days, median 10 days, bottom quarter 15 days on average.

sources.title: 5 strategies for a faster year-end close: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Annual close at site level: median 10 days for organisations under $100 million revenue and 23 days for $1 to $5 billion; fastest quarter 10 days or less; monthly reconciliations and a shared checklist help.

sources.title: Month-end close process and checklist
sources.supports: Steps: collect information, reconcile sub-ledgers with the general ledger, reconcile accounts starting with cash, inventory and fixed assets, prepare statements, final review by a controller not involved in the close; cites an APQC median close of 6.4 days.

sources.title: Building blocks of a successful financial close process (Kevin Kelso)
sources.supports: Close calendar with cut-off times, close instructions, daily close calls, exception hierarchy with materiality thresholds and an approval process for post-close adjustments, journal entry checklist with independent review as a detective control, standard JE templates, comparison with prior periods, post-mortem after each close.

sources.title: The monthly headache: how close management software can help (Mike Whitmire)
sources.supports: Close relies on disparate checklists, long email chains, status meetings and manual reconciliations between the ERP and Excel; SOX, IPO and audit work add time. Opinion piece by a close software vendor.

sources.title: Financial close management
sources.supports: Close steps: consolidating transactions, reconciliation, adjustments, trial balance check, fluctuation analysis comparing periods to find material changes, reporting under GAAP or IFRS.

sources.supports: Private industry: wages and salaries 70.5 percent and benefits 29.5 percent of total compensation.

assumptions: General workflow for one US operating entity of about 800 employees in a mid-size group; one close per month (cases_per_month = 1).
Loaded cost per hour = BLS May 2021 wage x 1.8 (benefits factor 1.43 from BLS ECEC December 2021, overhead factor 1.25 estimated).

The simulator adds every step's hands-on time to elapsed time, so steps that really run in parallel (s02 to s06, s12 with s14, s16 with s17) are summed. About 120 hands-on hours appear as about 5 days of elapsed time, which roughly matches several people working in parallel over the first five working days. Waits on concurrent steps are set near zero for this reason.

The simulated median (about 10 days, 1.6 times the benchmark) is above the APQC median of 6.4 days partly because this workflow starts at period end and includes the sub-ledger close before the trial balance, and partly because parallel work is summed; it is within the 0.5x to 2x check.
Reconciliation time uses APQC's 4-hour median per bank account and assumes 4 to 6 bank accounts plus about 65 other monthly reconciliations; balance sheet accounts reconciled quarterly are excluded.
Stated FTE on the process is higher than the hands-on time implies because close staff also do pre-close work, close meetings and checklist upkeep that are not modelled as steps.
Branch shares (late inputs, returns, adjustments, intercompany differences, group queries) are author estimates; no event log for the close was found.
The counterpart entity and the group reporting team are treated as outside parties with zero hands-on time in this workflow.
